SMTO-EXE-0262 — SMTO found more than one possible target and won't guess

GUID: 59d2bd56-e761-5822-8839-c5073bc146c4
Slug: recipe-resource-ambiguous
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: recipes

What happened

  • A workflow step needed one specific item, such as a file or record, but found several that match. SMTO stopped rather than risk picking the wrong one.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the run's conversation and see which step stopped and which items it found. Knowing the matching items shows you what makes the request unclear.
  2. Select Save to workflow on your original message. In the Prompt box, name the exact item, such as the full file path or record name, then select Save workflow. A precise name lets the step match exactly one item.
  3. Before running the new workflow, check in the conversation which steps already finished and what they changed. A new run starts from the beginning and could repeat those changes.

What success looks like

  • The step finishes and works on the item you intended.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workflow's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rerun the workflow unchanged; it will stop at the same point.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Workflow binding resolution found a list result that is not a single element at index 0, or capture matched a resource value to more than one earlier step's output.

What this means

  • Fresh result binding encountered a list other than a unique single element at index zero, or capture found multiple producer outputs matching a resource value. Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.

Why this can happen

  • Fresh result binding encountered a list other than a unique single element at index zero, or capture found multiple producer outputs matching a resource value.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the structured producer results and binding pointer to distinguish an empty, multiple or unsupported indexed selection.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the step's $step pointer and the source step's result (bindings.render), or the competing earlier outputs (recorder.extract). Refine the upstream query so it returns exactly one item, or bind an explicit unique identifier, then re-save the workflow.
  • Refine the source query or workflow binding until the intended resource is uniquely identified.

Retry and execution caution

  • Review the workflow and its current run evidence before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • A reviewed binding resolves exactly one intended resource from supported fresh evidence.

What not to do

  • Never repeat a write whose effect remains unknown.

Technical notes

  • Workflow diagnostics do not execute steps or grant approval. Preserve the pinned definition, original receipts, completed effects and any uncertainty; all execution uses the existing authorization boundary.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
